name: Tazarotenic acid
lead: Tazarotenic acid is the active form of tazarotene, a prescription topical retinoid used for acne, plaque psoriasis and signs of photoaging such as fine lines, wrinkles, uneven pigmentation and sun spots. Tazarotene is a prodrug: after it is applied, esterase enzymes in the skin and blood remove its ethyl ester group, producing the free acid that binds retinoic acid receptors [4][8][12]. People get tazarotenic acid only through tazarotene, sold under brand names such as Tazorac, Arazlo and Fabior and as generics [12].

The appearance chain is direct. Tazarotene is converted to tazarotenic acid, which acts on receptors that govern how skin cells grow and differentiate, and in a 12-month trial in people with facial photodamage the cream improved fine wrinkling, mottled pigmentation and sun spots compared with vehicle [3][4]. Acne improvement is also documented [9][12].

Tazarotenic acid binds retinoic acid receptors (RARs) but not retinoid X receptors, and in laboratory assays it is selective for the RAR-beta and RAR-gamma subtypes [1][4]. In online skincare discussion, tazarotene is described by some users as a stronger alternative to tretinoin for texture and anti-aging. No published study has tested tazarotenic acid as a stand-alone cosmetic ingredient; the human evidence concerns the parent drug.

paras: Tazarotene is approved for acne and plaque psoriasis and can reduce photoaging signs including fine lines, wrinkles, hyperpigmentation and lentigines; Wikipedia notes that daily sunscreen use improves results [12]. In acne it is often combined with benzoyl peroxide or an oral antibiotic, and in psoriasis it is paired with a corticosteroid, which can also reduce irritation [12].

Tazarotene was first approved as a gel in 1997, followed by 0.05% and 0.1% creams in 2000, a 0.1% foam in 2012 and a 0.045% lotion in 2019, and a fixed-dose combination with halobetasol (Duobrii) is approved for psoriasis [12].

Retinoids are grouped by generation. Tretinoin and isotretinoin are first-generation natural retinoic acids; adapalene, bexarotene and tazarotene are third-generation synthetic benzoic acid derivatives; and trifarotene, approved in the US in 2019, is a fourth-generation compound selective for RAR-gamma [100]. Tazarotene's narrower receptor targeting differs from the broader RAR and RXR binding of the natural acids [100][12]. Retinoic acid signalling is central to regulating skin cell growth and differentiation [100].

Tazarotene belongs to the acetylenic retinoids, a class whose structure resists isomerization. Its free acid, tazarotenic acid, binds RARs and not RXRs, and gene-activation assays indicate selectivity for the RAR-beta and RAR-gamma subtypes [1][4]. Through these receptors it is described as slowing keratinocyte proliferation and promoting differentiation, and reviews also discuss comedolytic and anti-inflammatory properties of topical retinoids [7][12].

After topical application, only a few percent of the dose reaches the stratum corneum and viable epidermis, and a review of the drug's pharmacokinetics describes limited absorption into the bloodstream, with less than about 6% of the applied dose absorbed [2][5]. Tazarotene is converted by esterases in human blood and liver to tazarotenic acid [8]. Tazarotenic acid is then further metabolized, with cytochrome P450 2C8 and flavin-containing monooxygenases implicated in humans [6]. Over 99% is bound to plasma proteins and it is eliminated in urine and feces [12].
No studies found of tazarotenic acid administered on its own. Human trials have tested its parent drug, tazarotene.

In a 24-week double-blind trial of 563 people with facial photodamage, followed by a 28-week open-label extension, 0.1% tazarotene cream produced significantly more improvement than vehicle in fine wrinkling, mottled hyperpigmentation, lentigines and other signs; improvement had not plateaued by week 52. Twenty of 283 tazarotene-treated participants and 1 of 280 vehicle participants stopped because of adverse events, and plasma tazarotenic acid stayed at or below 0.71 ng/mL [3]. Pooled results of two vehicle-controlled trials examined 0.1% tazarotene cream in facial acne [9]. Registered trials have also looked at tazarotene in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and scalp psoriasis [11][13].

Skin irritation (redness, itching, burning) is the most commonly reported effect of tazarotene and tends to rise with concentration [12]. A review of tazarotene safety concluded that systemic exposure is minimal and found no association with contact sensitization, phototoxicity or carcinogenicity [5]. Tazarotene is nonetheless labelled as contraindicated in pregnancy, a position based on animal studies [12].

The FDA originally classed tazarotene as Category X, stricter than the Category C given to adapalene and tretinoin, and after lettered categories were dropped in 2015 it was still deemed contraindicated, based on animal teratogenicity data because human pregnancy data are lacking [12]. The American Academy of Dermatology advises against topical retinoids in pregnancy, and a 2026 Nordic cohort study reported no rise in birth defects with topical retinoid use [100].

Users of prescription retinoids discuss tazarotene as a step up in strength from tretinoin or adapalene, and are more likely to talk about the brand-name product than about the metabolite. Its irritation profile, which Wikipedia says increases with concentration, is a frequent topic [12].

Preclinical work suggests tazarotene may slow melanoma growth through tazarotene-induced genes (TIG1, TIG2, TIG3), by suppressing mTOR signalling and promoting differentiation and immune-cell recruitment; this is early-stage laboratory research [12]. Researchers have developed nanoparticle formulations of tazarotene intended to deliver it to hair follicles in inflammatory skin disease [10].

timeline.event: Tazarotene described in the literature as a receptor-selective retinoid whose acid form binds RARs [1].
12-month photodamage trial of 0.1% tazarotene cream published [3].
FDA retires lettered pregnancy categories; tazarotene remains contraindicated in pregnancy [12].

lore.intro: Tazarotenic acid is rarely named in community discussion; posts focus on tazarotene itself as a potent prescription retinoid for skin texture and aging.

claims.claim: Tazarotene is a stronger anti-aging retinoid than tretinoin
claims.believers: Proponents of prescription retinoids describe tazarotene as more potent, citing its receptor selectivity.
claims.experts: Trials show tazarotene improves photodamage versus vehicle [3]; no head-to-head comparison with tretinoin was found among the published studies reviewed.

claims.claim: The metabolite is where the activity comes from
claims.believers: Users reading drug references note that tazarotene is a prodrug.
claims.experts: Pharmacology studies confirm that esterases convert tazarotene to tazarotenic acid, which binds RARs [4][8].

claims.claim: Tazarotene is irritating, so it must be eased into
claims.believers: Retinoid users commonly describe redness and peeling at the start and combine it with moisturisers or corticosteroids in psoriasis.
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports irritation is the most common adverse effect, usually mild to moderate and increasing with concentration; pairing with a corticosteroid can reduce it in psoriasis [12].

card.summary: The active acid form of prescription tazarotene; evidence exists for the parent retinoid's photoaging effect, not for the metabolite alone.
card.aka: Active metabolite of tazarotene (Tazorac, Arazlo, Fabior)
card.note: Parent drug is contraindicated in pregnancy; irritation is common.

quick.overview:
Tazarotenic acid is what the body makes from tazarotene, a prescription topical retinoid used for acne, psoriasis and photodamage. It is not sold on its own.

A 12-month trial of tazarotene cream showed improvement in wrinkles and pigmentation versus vehicle. No studies have tested the acid alone.
quick.mechanism: Skin and blood esterases convert tazarotene to tazarotenic acid, which binds retinoic acid receptors, selectively RAR-beta and RAR-gamma, altering keratinocyte growth and differentiation.
quick.risks: Irritation is the most common effect of the parent drug. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Prescription-only in the US.

angle.text: Tazarotenic acid is what makes tazarotene work: it is the receptor-binding form. A 12-month trial of tazarotene 0.1% cream reported improvement in fine wrinkling and mottled pigmentation versus vehicle [3].
